source.title: Pathologies of Predictive Diversity in Deep Ensembles
source.authors: T. Abe; E. Kelly Buchanan; Geoff Pleiss; J. Cunningham

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test performance across model-width sweeps and discusses the interpolation threshold, but its ensemble-focused setup differs from the claim versions' specified experiments.
record.gate_note: Most results concern predictive diversity in ensembles, outside the listed claim versions. The width sweeps and interpolation discussion bear on V2; many other findings are not rows because they measure ensemble diversity or ensemble performance under interventions rather than a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study's width sweeps report ensemble cross-entropy and average component cross-entropy, rather than classification test error after reaching zero training error as named by V2. Its own component-model double-descent observation is relevant context, but does not establish that outcome. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete: diversity encouragement can benefit small classification ensembles while harming large ones; diversity discouragement is often benign for large ensembles. Selecting better component models generally provides greater gains than selecting for predictive diversity, including when diversity is available through heterogeneous architectures.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines predictive diversity and ensemble performance, including capacity sweeps, rather than the original claim's individual-network generalization-gap experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Component-model capacity changes how predictive diversity relates to ensemble performance; random-feature ensemble diversity changes around the interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-feature ensembles improve monotonically in test cross-entropy with width. Average component cross-entropy exhibits double descent, while diversity increases before interpolation and decreases afterward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width can improve ensemble probabilistic performance through different component-performance and diversity trade-offs before and after interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet ensembles improve in test cross-entropy with increasing width or depth; sufficiently large components improve while becoming less diverse. The interpolation transition cannot be conclusively identified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing ResNet capacity can improve ensemble probabilistic performance despite decreasing predictive diversity.

record.problems: The capacity-sweep findings are mainly shown in figures without numeric values in the text. For ResNets, the authors say regularization prevents a conclusive identification of the transition point. The results concern ensemble cross-entropy, not the individual-network training-to-test error gap specified in V2.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Other reported ensemble diversity and accuracy results do not measure a behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Matched random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy.

Individual-network classification test error as width increases beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold. Component cross-entropy double descent is reported for random-feature classifiers, but classification-error results are not supplied; the ResNet interpolation threshold is inconclusive.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly describes V2 as a training-to-test generalization-gap claim. V2 concerns test error versus width after interpolation. Differences in architecture alone would permit a new-setting test; the decisive limitations here are the reported outcome and the unestablished ResNet interpolation threshold.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.

The study does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained to convergence without explicit regularization on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; it reports ensemble cross-entropy sweeps for random-feature classifiers on MNIST and ResNets on CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected model comparisons are not tested.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization are not tested.
Large-batch training effects are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization-gap comparisons are not tested.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy are not tested.

rows.subject: random feature models
rows.size_stated: Classifier width varied; specific widths not stated in text.
rows.operation_detail: Compared random-feature classifier ensembles across widths on MNIST.

conditions.value: varied; specific values not stated in text

rows.measure: Ensemble test cross-entropy/performance as a function of classifier width; figure-only values.
rows.note: The text says ensemble performance improves monotonically with width and component-model performance shows double descent, but does not give numeric values or identify the test-error gap.
rows.check: Ensemble cross-entropy cannot establish individual-network classification error beyond the interpolation threshold. Section 5.2 separately reports double descent in average component cross-entropy; these are random Fourier features fitted with logistic regression (Appendix B.3). The reported ensemble improvement is clear, so 'partial' should not represent uncertainty about its relevance to V2.

rows.subject: ResNet models
rows.size_stated: Width varied; specific widths not stated in text.
rows.operation_detail: Compared ensembles of ResNets with increasing width on CIFAR10.
rows.note: Text says increasing width yields better ensembles; the interpolation transition point is not conclusively identified for ResNets.
rows.check: Ensemble cross-entropy does not establish V2's individual-network classification-error trend after interpolation; the authors explicitly cannot identify the ResNet transition conclusively. Appendix B.4 specifies channel multipliers of 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1, 2 and 4. Training uses regularization and a fixed schedule, rather than demonstrated convergence.

rows.subject: ResNet models
rows.size_stated: Depth varied; specific depths not stated in text.
rows.operation_detail: Compared ensembles of ResNets with increasing depth on CIFAR10.
rows.note: This is a depth sweep, not the width manipulation named by V2; included as a related capacity sweep. Text says increasing depth yields better ensembles, while transition point is inconclusive.
rows.check: Depth is not the width manipulation named by V2, and ensemble cross-entropy is not its classification-error outcome. Appendix B.4 specifies n = 1 through 7 for the depth sweep, contradicting the row's statement that depths are unspecified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Random-feature ensembles on MNIST; ResNet ensembles on CIFAR10
reader_labels.reason: Ensemble performance improves with width, but the reported outcome is ensemble cross-entropy and does not establish the claimed test-error gap behavior; the ResNet transition point is also inconclusive (R1–R3).
